block_size.markdownDescription: Number of ports reserved for each lane. By default devlanes counts the ports the config needs and adds half again, rounded up to ten. A fixed size smaller than what the config needs is an error.

ReadyCheck.markdownDescription: Readiness probe: exactly one of `tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd`, retried until it passes or `timeout` runs out.

cmd.description: Ready once this command exits 0. It runs on the host through `/bin/sh` (a list is quoted into one command line) with its output discarded, is retried until the timeout, and each attempt is cut off after 10 seconds. http.description: Ready once a GET request to `path` on the unit's main port answers with `status`, or with a 2xx status when `status` is unset. Redirects are not followed. Best when the app has a health route that fails while it is broken.

log.markdownDescription: Ready once a line of output matches this regular expression, with colors and other terminal escape codes removed; recent lines printed before the check began count too. Suits workers without a port: have them print a line once connected.

With `replicas`, the service starts all its copies when any copy's expression gives true. Defaults to true.

hidden.markdownDescription: Keep this service's ports and hosts off machines connected with `devlanes remote connect`: they are not mirrored there and cannot be reached from there. The service still runs and works on this machine. Defaults to false.

hosts.description: Hostnames the devlanes HTTPS proxy routes to this service, so `https://<host>` reaches it. One entry or a list; an entry is a hostname or a mapping with `host` and optional `port` (a named port), `fallback` and `host_header`. A `*.` wildcard matches subdomains, and an exact host wins over it. The first non-wildcard host becomes `public_url`, non-wildcard hosts join the lane's `DEVLANES_ORIGINS`, and having hosts makes the default `ready` a TCP check. Keep them under `${{ lane.domain }}` so lanes do not collide.

ready.description: When the service counts as up: `devlanes start` waits for it, and `after: services` tasks run once every started service is ready. Write `started` (ready once the process runs) or a mapping with one of `tcp`, `http`, `log` or `cmd`, plus `timeout` (default 60s). Without it, a service with `hosts` waits for TCP on its port and one without hosts uses `started`. A check that times out marks the service failed, which also skips `after: services` tasks; the process keeps running and is not restarted.

replicas.description: Number of copies of this service to run, each with its own port, for example several queue workers. A plain number of at least 1, the same in every lane, because each copy reserves ports in every lane's block; `${{ ... }}` expressions are not allowed. Defaults to 1.

A plain number of at least 1, the same in every lane, because each copy reserves ports in every lane's block; `${{ ... }}` expressions are not allowed. Defaults to 1.

run.description: Command that starts the service. A string runs with `/bin/sh -c`, so pipes, `&&` and multi-line scripts work; a list is an argv run directly without a shell. It starts in the lane's worktree root unless `cwd` is set. devlanes runs it exactly as written, so it cannot be combined with `preset`; prefer `run_script` when the command is a script in a project file. Exactly one of `run` and `run_script` is required after templates are applied.

templates.description: Named service settings that services reuse with `extends: <template>`. The service inherits every setting of the template and its own settings win: mappings (`env`, `ready`, `stop`, preset options, `run_script`) merge by key, lists (`tags`, `hosts`, `sync`) and single values replace. Setting `run` or `run_script` drops the inherited other one, and one `ready` probe (`tcp`, `http`, `log`, `cmd`) drops the inherited probe. Templates may extend other templates, are never started themselves, and are applied after `devlanes.local.yaml` is merged.
